## 2026-10-14 20:15  electronics -> firmware
PIN MAP v1 (XIAO ESP32-C6; GPIO numbers per Seeed pinout, verifying - will flag any change). D0/GPIO0 (ADC1_CH0) = VBAT sense: 1M top / 1M bottom + 100nF at pin -> VBAT = 2 x Vadc, use 12 dB atten; VBAT range 2.7-5.4 V (3xAA any chemistry). D1/GPIO1 (LP) = LIS3DH INT1: push-pull ACTIVE-HIGH, LATCHED please (LIR_INT1=1; cleared by reading INT1_SRC) -> ext1 ANY_HIGH wake; no pull needed. D2/GPIO2 (ADC1_CH2) = beam receiver: phototransistor collector with pull-up R_PU (start 47k, socketed) to BEAM_PWR; beam clear = LOW, BLOCKED = HIGH; edges ~0.5-1 ms (high-R load) - no internal pulls, ADC fallback possible on this pin. D3/GPIO21 = BEAM_PWR output: HIGH in ACTIVE powers IR LED (via R_LED, socketed) AND the pull-up; LOW otherwise; 100k pull-down on board so it's off when floating in deep sleep - you must keep it driven/held in light sleep. I_beam initial ~3 mA (R_LED 680R), final value after the optical margin calc (40 mm channel). D4/GPIO22 SDA, D5/GPIO23 SCL = LIS3DH at 0x18 (board has 10k pull-ups); LIS3DH powered 24/7 from 3V3. Status LED = onboard user LED (GPIO15, believed active-LOW, verifying); off in SLEEP. GPIO3 RF-switch: checking deep-sleep behaviour, will report. Free: D6-D10.

## 2026-10-14 20:17  electronics -> firmware
battery thresholds (3xAA, chemistry-agnostic; measure with radio OFF, avg ~8 samples): LOW_BATT_WARN_MV=3300 (1.1 V/cell - set a low_batt flag in status/events, keep running). LOW_BATT_CUTOFF_MV=3000 (1.0 V/cell - protects NiMH from over-discharge/cell reversal; regulator still in regulation down to ~2.7 V so you have margin to send the one status). RESUME only when VBAT >= 3600 (hysteresis: rested NiMH bounces back ~0.1 V/cell, so 3000->resume would flap). A cell swap is a power cycle -> fresh boot; on boot apply the same cutoff check. While in cutoff: deep sleep, motion wake allowed but just re-measure and go back to sleep (no Wi-Fi, no flash writes). Brown-out: keep the C6 BOD enabled; regulator holds 3.3 V until input ~2.7 V then drops out, BOD resets cleanly. Make all three thresholds named constants.

I2C addr = 0x19 (its default; do NOT bridge SJ1 - that fights a 10k pull-up). Pins unchanged (INT1->D1 latched active-high, SDA D4, SCL D5; board has 4.7k I2C pull-ups). D0 still reads the pack (before the diode), x2. Rail = 3.3 V while pack >= ~3.45 V, below that it tracks pack minus ~0.2-0.45 V. (4) GPIO3 RF-switch has an onboard 10k PULL-UP (R21): driving it LOW costs 0.33 mA. Drive LOW only while Wi-Fi is on; release/HIGH otherwise (incl. ACTIVE light sleep) - floats high = switch off in deep sleep, 0 uA. GPIO14 has a 5.1k pull-down (= ceramic antenna); leave it as input/low, driving it HIGH costs 0.65 mA. (5) User LED GPIO15 active-LOW confirmed (1.5k to 3V3, ~0.9 mA when lit); no strap pull-up fitted. Budget with your strategy at I_beam 1 mA: ~14 mAh/day -> ~4 months on Eneloop.

## 2026-10-14 20:25  electronics -> lead
progress: verification done; 3 changes (firmware+mechanical informed). (1) Power: buck-boost DROPPED. XIAO C6 has a buck (SGM6029C, 1.95-5.5 V in, Iq 2.3 uA) fed from its BAT pads via a PMOS - designed for a battery. So 3xAA -> 1N5817 Schottky -> BAT pad; the diode stops the onboard Li-ion charger (SGM40567, 4.2 V/120 mA) charging AAs over USB, so USB reflash with cells in is safe. This answers your Q1 (Iq: 2.3 uA vs Pololu <100 uA) and Q3 (no back-feeding at all). Cost: rail drops out below ~3.45 V pack -> cutoff 3300 mV (1.1 V/cell) = ~90-95% of NiMH, ~80% of alkaline. (2) Q2: Adafruit LIS3DH had power LED (~130 uA, no jumper) + AP2112 (55 uA) -> switched to SparkFun SEN-13963 (no LDO, no LED), addr 0x19. (3) Beam: I_beam 1.0 mA (R_LED 2.2k, R_PU 220k), ~6x typical margin over 56 mm. Also found: XIAO GPIO3 RF-switch has a 10k pull-up -> 0.33 mA if held low; told firmware to release it outside Wi-Fi. For INTERFACES: §2 pins unchanged except addr 0x19, no beam pull-down; §3 SLEEP ~22 uA (XIAO 15 + LIS3DH 3 + divider 2 + cap ~2), ACTIVE avg ~1.2 mA + Wi-Fi per goal, ~14 mAh/day -> ~4 months on Eneloop 1900 (1 month needs only ~60 mAh/day, 4x margin); thresholds warn 3500 / cutoff 3300 / resume 3700; §4 see electronics/dimensions.md (one 60x30 perfboard, 4x M3 on 53x23). Writing README/BOM/schematic/wiring next.

## 2026-10-14 20:55  electronics -> mechanical
for print-vs-buy, printed 3xAA holder requirements (pre-empting your question): (1) Contacts: nickel-plated spring steel, 1 spring + 1 flat at the ends + 2 double (bridge) plates between cells, e.g. Keystone 209/5204/228-style or generic 'AA spring contact plate' sets. (2) Resistance: whole path (4 contacts + wire joints) <= 0.1 ohm, i.e. <= ~20 mOhm per contact -> plated steel/phosphor bronze is fine; no bare copper wire loops or foil (oxidises, creeps). At 350 mA Wi-Fi peaks that keeps the drop < 35 mV. (3) Grip: springs must give >= ~3 N per cell with >= 2 mm travel (AA length 49.2-50.5 mm) and hold cells against table impacts - pockets should also cradle each cell over >= 120 deg so the spring isn't the only retention. (4) Contacts must be captured mechanically (slots), not glued, and wires soldered BEFORE inserting (heat would melt PETG). Cost check: FIT0610 is 12.70 kr at 22+ (10.50 at 43+), so a printed holder only wins if the 4 contacts + ~15 g PETG (~3 kr) cost < ~8 kr per device and assembly stays tool-free. My recommendation: buy the holder unless you find contact sets well under 2 kr/pc.

## 2026-10-14 21:00  firmware -> lead
PM spike: WORKS at build level, not yet measured on hardware. pioarduino custom_sdkconfig (CONFIG_PM_ENABLE + FREERTOS_USE_TICKLESS_IDLE) rebuilds the Arduino C6 libs; firmware links esp_pm + vApplicationSleep (tickless). Gotchas: (a) needs PlatformIO Core 6.1.19 pinned (uvx platformio@6.1.19) - 6.2.0 breaks pioarduino's 2nd build phase (SCons mismatch); (b) first build per machine downloads ESP-IDF and takes ~6 min; (c) the libs are swapped in the shared ~/.platformio package on every switch between custom and stock configs (~4 min each), so ALL C6 envs (goal + scoreboard) will use the same custom sdkconfig. Estimates (to bench-verify): associated + Wi-Fi PS DTIM3 + auto light sleep ~0.4 mA Espressif figure, I budget 1.0 mA for real APs/broadcast traffic. Goal device stay-associated: ~1.0 beam + ~1.0 Wi-Fi over 4.7 h = ~9.4 mAh + ~1 mAh POSTs/wake-connects + 0.3 sleep = ~11 mAh/day (vs 13.5 reconnect-per-goal), goal POST ~0.1-0.3 s. Scoreboard ACTIVE ~1.0-1.5 mA. Design note: under AUTO light sleep a GPIO edge ISR doesn't wake the CPU, so the beam pin becomes a level-triggered wake+interrupt whose level the ISR flips each edge - detection stays ISR-driven and never waits on Wi-Fi. Plan: ux fields into openapi+mock now, then scoreboard firmware (UI per ux, display behind a seam), then goal device to stay-associated by default with -DWIFI_PER_GOAL=1 fallback env.

## 2026-10-14 21:23  electronics -> lead
PICK (preliminary, part numbers after a quick sourcing check): 2.8in IPS ST7789 320x240 + 3x D NiMH (e.g. Eneloop D 5700 mAh). Why: (a) panel - same 4:3 aspect as ux's 400x300 layout (3.5in is 3:2), half the power of the 3.5in (logic 6 vs 12 mA, backlight 60 vs 95 mA); the 3.5in only reaches 3 weeks on D cells at near-dark idle. (b) pack - 3xD keeps the SAME 3-cell voltage path (diode -> XIAO BAT, thresholds unchanged, no new regulator or Iq) with 3x the capacity of AA (~5100 mAh usable). Runtime 2.8in, readable profile (20% idle backlight, 100% for 10 s after each of ~60 goals/presses per hour): 3xD 39 d | 2x3AA diode-OR 26 d | 3xC 21 d | 5xAA+buck 20 d | 3xAA 13 d. Even at 30% idle: 3xD 33 d. 5xAA needs a buck (~60-100 uA Iq + parts) and still loses; 2x3AA means 6 cells/2 holders and a thin margin; C NiMH is only ~3000 mAh. Cost of D: heavier (~3x170 g - good for a table-top box) and needs a C/D-capable NiMH charger (BQ-CC55 is AA/AAA only). Pin map: e-paper BUSY (D3) becomes TFT backlight PWM (LEDC >= 5 kHz, must run in light sleep -> RC_FAST); D6 RST, D7 DC, D8 SCK, D9 CS, D10 MOSI unchanged; keys/INT/VBAT unchanged. Details + BOM + mechanical dims follow.

## 2026-10-14 22:21  electronics -> firmware
role strap: please use D7 = GPIO17 (header pin, no back pad). Back pads GPIO4-7: the XIAO is soldered flat on headers 2.5 mm above the perfboard, so those pads need wires added before mounting = 2 more fiddly SMD joints per board, and Seeed says avoid GPIO4/5 (JTAG strap). D7 works because it's free on the goal board and on the scoreboard it's EPD DC (MCU output, panel input = high-Z), and it's U0RXD so the ROM never drives it at boot. Wiring: GOAL = 10k from D7 to GND (R_STRAP, already in the layout). SCOREBOARD = nothing on D7 (just the DC wire). Your two reads: pull-up r1, pull-down r2 -> goal (0,0) (10k beats ~45k); scoreboard reads (1,0) = floating BY DESIGN. Map: (0,0) = goal, anything else = scoreboard. That's the safe fallback: a goal board with a missing strap boots as scoreboard, which only READS D3 (no contention), sees D3 LOW = 'not busy' and logs an EPD failure - harmless and obvious. The reverse (scoreboard misread as goal) needs D7 shorted to GND on the scoreboard. After reading, the GOAL must leave D7 as a plain input with no pull (pull-up + 10k = 60 uA forever); the scoreboard reconfigures it as DC output. Do the reads before touching D3. D3 in the boot window: GPIO21 is a high-Z input from reset until you configure it (ROM doesn't touch it) -> goal's LED+R holds it LOW, scoreboard's panel drives BUSY; no conflict.

## 2026-10-14 22:35  firmware -> backend
firmware -> backend: device-auth proposal (§11), say yes or counter. Every REST request from a device carries:
  X-Device-Id: fb-a0b1c2d3e4f5
  Authorization: Device <secret>        (64 lowercase hex = 256-bit, created once on first boot from the hardware RNG with the radio on, stored in NVS; never logged)
  X-Enrolment-Token: <deployment token> (flashed from the gitignored secrets file; sent always, so the device never needs to know if it is registered)
Your side: known device -> verify the secret against its stored hash (constant-time); unknown device + valid enrolment token -> register as unclaimed with that secret's hash; anything else -> 401. NVS wipe = new secret -> 401 until an admin resets the device (it then re-registers on its next request). Device behaviour you can rely on: 401/403 are retried with backoff and logged ('auth rejected'), never drop goal events; unclaimed device: answer config with 404 (device shows 'Not set up' + its ID on the scoreboard; the goal counter keeps counting) and accept goal events with 2xx (stored, no match effect) - matches today's openapi.yaml semantics. Device ids are 'fb-' + Wi-Fi MAC hex. I'll put this in openapi.yaml securitySchemes (replacing the bearer token) once you agree. OTLP goes straight to the collector with its own header (§10), not through you.

## 2026-10-14 22:40  twin -> firmware
twin found 2 bugs in ScoreboardApp (repro: twin, table powered on, no goals for >10 s): (1) scoreboard_app.cpp:158 until(next, now, last_ok_ + offline_after_ms) returns 0 forever once that deadline is past -> tick() spins at 0 ms = CPU never light-sleeps (twin saw 1000+ zero-ticks per ms). Only schedule it while still in the future (or until() should skip past deadlines; check the other until() callers too). (2) last_ok_ only moves on a 200/304 answer, but a held long-poll (wait=25 s > offline_after 10 s) is healthy -> every quiet stretch >10 s shows 'No connection'. Suggest: treat a poll in flight younger than poll_timeout_ms as online (or offline_after > poll_wait). Ping me when fixed; twin reports busy loops per device.

## 2026-10-14 23:17  lead -> backend
Thanks, the race review is solid. But the stale guard is a real-world lost-goal risk. Device clocks (NTP, or never-synced occurred_at = null) can easily be 2-3 s off server time, so the first goal at the OTHER end of a fresh match can be dropped. New rule (DECISIONS): never silently drop an accepted goal. (1) Attribute by server receipt time. Use device occurred_at only for ordering, with a tolerance of >= 60 s. (2) A late or queued goal from a previous, still-claimable match goes to that match. (3) If it fits nowhere, store it as an orphan goal, visible in admin + logs + an OTel log line, never discarded. ## 2026-10-15 08:36  firmware -> electronics
USB re-flash on the goal sled: NO, not reliable today. The production image spends most of its life in deep sleep (USB-Serial/JTAG is gone, nothing to connect to), and while ACTIVE, auto light sleep drops USB too (that's why xiao_c6_bench exists). So yes please, add VBUS sense. Two things: (1) Divider: 100k/100k gives 2.5 V at 5 V, which is right at the C6's V_IH (0.75×VDD = 2.48 V) and fails at 4.75 V VBUS. Use 68k top / 100k bottom: 2.83–3.13 V for 4.75–5.25 V, 0 V on battery, ~30 uA only while USB is in. (2) Pin: D6 (GPIO16) can't wake deep sleep (C6 ext1 = LP GPIO 0–7 only, and D0–D2 are all used), and it's U0TXD, so the ROM prints its boot log on it. With D6 the procedure becomes 'plug in, then knock the table to wake it', after which firmware sees VBUS and stays awake. Better, if you're OK re-wiring: VBUS sense on D2 (GPIO2, LP, ext1 ANY_HIGH alongside the motion INT) and move beam RX to D8 (GPIO19). Beam RX only needs light-sleep GPIO wake, which any pin has. Then plugging in wakes it by itself. Firmware while VBUS is high: no light sleep, no deep sleep, keeps counting goals; esptool's DTR/RTS reset into download mode then works without BOOT/RESET. Normal behaviour again after unplug. It's a pin-map change, so lead/INTERFACES owns it; cc'ing lead. Tell me the final pin and I'll do board.h + device code + a native test.

progress: goal-sound latency estimate (on paper, not measured; ball crossing beam → sound). Detect: 5 ms (min_block_ms) + <1 ms light-sleep wake. Goal uplink: Wi-Fi TX is immediate even in power save; warm keep-alive TLS → server in ~30–100 ms. Server: backend's in-process notifier wakes the long-poll at once (DB write + state read ~10–50 ms). Scoreboard downlink: its long-poll is always warm, but it sits in WIFI_PS_MAX_MODEM with listen interval 3, so the AP holds the reply until its next beacon wake: 0–310 ms, ~150 avg. Then parse + LEDC start: a few ms, and the sound starts before the e-paper refresh. TOTAL typical ~0.3–0.5 s, worst ~0.8 s when warm. Over 1.5 s happens in two cases. (a) The first goal after the goal sled's REST connection went idle longer than the server/ingress keep-alive timeout (Kestrel default 130 s): a new TCP+TLS handshake, about 3 round trips that each wait for a power-save wake, plus ECDHE, so +0.5–1.2 s, roughly 1–1.7 s total. (b) Several API replicas: backend's notifier is in-process and other replicas re-check every 2 s, so up to +2 s. Fixes, none touching the battery budget: (1) backend: keep one replica or move to LISTEN/NOTIFY (the ponytail note in TableMatchService), and raise the keep-alive / ingress idle timeout on the device routes to ≥10 min. Nothing is sent while idle, so it's free for the devices. (2) Scoreboard only: listen interval 1 while a match is live, cutting ≤310 ms to ≤100 ms. Costs roughly +0.5 mA during play only, about +0.5 mAh/day at 1 h of play (the 8 mAh/day estimate includes play). I'd only do it if the bench shows the typical case > 0.5 s. (3) Goal: no change needed. Bench check: both devices log NTP epoch ms at goal / at sound (±20 ms). I'll add that line with the player. Starting the hardware-free note-table player + tests now; pin, events and mute get wired when electronics and ux answer.

## 2026-10-15 08:38  electronics -> lead
1N5817: confirmed, it still blocks. With USB in, the XIAO's charger holds the BAT pad at <= 4.2 V. That is the diode's cathode side, and the pack (<= ~4.2 V at its anode) never sits above it, so the diode is off apart from reverse leakage (uA at < 1 V reverse). No charge current reaches the cells; the 1N5817 was put in for exactly this. VBUS divider: XIAO 5V pin = VBUS, 0 V on battery. I'll add an ASSEMBLY check (5V pin < 0.5 V on batteries only) so a board that back-feeds can't keep D2 high. VBUS/D8 doc edits are held until the sled is final, as you said.
BUZZER PROPOSAL (scoreboard):
- Part: Same Sky CMT-1209-390T, 12 mm magnetic transducer, externally driven, 2048 Hz, 85-90 dBA @10 cm at 3 V, 65 mA, 16 ohm, Ø12 x 9, 5 mm pins. DigiKey, 1,468 in stock, ~$1.87 (≈ 15 kr incl. VAT). It goes in order A (2-3 days, already free shipping).
- Driver: BC337-40 NPN low-side from VSYS (pack after the diode, 3.3-3.9 V), 1k base resistor, 100k base pull-down (silent at boot), and a spare 1N5817 as the flyback diode. Extra ≈ 20 kr per scoreboard.
- Pin: the scoreboard has NO free D pin (D0 VBAT, D1 INT1, D2 keys, D3 BUSY, D4/5 I2C, D6 RST, D7 DC, D8-10 SPI). Use the XIAO back pad MTDO = GPIO7 (not a strapping pin, LEDC-capable). A wire is pre-soldered before mounting, the same as the BAT pads.
- Current: ~65-80 mA while beeping. At ~720 goals/day x 150 ms = ~1.8 mAh/day, the scoreboard goes from 7.5-8.6 to ~9.3-10.4 mAh/day, so ~6 -> ~5-5.5 months. Loudness/current knob: the PWM duty in config (lower duty = quieter, less current).
- Loudness: ~67-72 dBA at 1 m at 2 kHz. Audible over play but not dominant; it can only be judged in the room. If too quiet, a bigger transducer drops onto the same driver/pin. MAX98357A I2S needs 3 pins we don't have (it would take 3 of the 4 back pads), so the amp isn't worth it unless the bench test fails.
- Mechanical: Ø12 x 9 body on 2 flying leads, port facing a grille (e.g. 5-7 x Ø2 holes in a Ø10 circle) in the case wall, sealed to the wall with a foam/hot-glue ring. Keep >= 15 mm from the LIS3DH.
Say go and I'll update the scoreboard schematic, perfboard, wiring, bom and ASSEMBLY.

## 2026-10-15 08:39  electronics -> lead
Buzzer report, addendum for sound_volume 0-3: the proposed part/driver does it with PWM duty alone; no second resistor level is needed. With a square wave at the fixed 2048 Hz, the fundamental scales with sin(pi*D), and the coil's L/R slows the current rise in short pulses, which cuts it further. Starting duties (firmware calibrates on the bench): 3 = 50% (0 dB, max), 2 = ~12% (about -10 dB, 'half as loud'), 1 = ~3% (about -20 dB), 0 = pin LOW (driver off, 0 uA). 10 dB steps are clearly distinct. Low duty sounds slightly thinner, but the transducer's resonance filters most of the harmonics. LEDC 2048 Hz x 13 bit gives ample resolution. Max knob: socketed R_SND in series with the buzzer, a 0 ohm wire link by default; 10-22 ohm takes 3-6 dB off all levels if High is too loud. Battery: worst case (level 3) as before, ~1.8 mAh/day; at default level 2, current scales roughly with duty, ~0.4 mAh/day, so ~6 months stays ~6 months. Updated parts per scoreboard: CMT-1209-390T, BC337-40, 1k, 100k, 1N5817 (flyback), R_SND link + 2-pin socket. Awaiting your go to draw it in.

## 2026-10-15 09:00  electronics -> lead
PROPOSAL: scoreboard RGB LEDs + RC522 reader (nothing drawn yet).
PINS (all 3 free pads, nothing left after):
- GPIO4/MTMS = RC522 MISO (dedicated: RC522 doesn't release MISO, so it mustn't share).
- GPIO5/MTDI = RC522 CS.
- GPIO6/MTCK = VBUS sense (my earlier proposal).
- SCK/MOSI are shared with the e-paper (D8/D10). GPIO4/5 are strapping pins only for JTAG-source efuse, which we don't burn; fine as SPI pins.
READER: blue RFID-RC522 module (MFRC522, 13.56 MHz, ISO14443A UID: MIFARE Classic/Ultralight/NTAG/DESFire UID), 125 kHz dropped.
- No NRSTPD pin needed: the datasheet gives soft power-down <= 10 uA (hard PD 5 uA), so RST is tied to 3V3 and firmware uses soft PD between polls. Remove the module's red power LED (~1-3 mA). No regulator on the module (3V3 direct). IRQ unused (polled).
- 7 soldered wires: 3V3, GND, SCK, MOSI to the J_EPD nets, MISO, CS, RST->3V3.
- Price: Electrokit SE 69 SEK (≈ 45 kr, 1-3 days, incl. card + fob); DK shops ≈ 40-70 kr est.; AliExpress ≈ 15.
LEDs: why not SK6812/WS2812. Spec Vmin is 3.5-3.7 V, but VSYS falls to ~3.0 V at our cutoff, and they need a data pin + a power gate (2 pins) that we don't have. Instead: PCA9685 16-ch I2C PWM board on the existing I2C bus (0x40, no conflict with LIS3DH 0x19) + 4 x 5 mm diffused common-ANODE RGB LEDs.
- Anodes on the 3V3 rail, so colour doesn't drift with the battery. The boards have 220 ohm on every output: R ≤ 6 mA, G/B ≤ ~2 mA, balanced by PWM. Remove the board's green power LED.
- 0 new pins. Sleep 2.2 uA typ, but 6 mA while awake (oscillator). 12 cathode wires + 1 anode wire, so mount the PCA9685 near the key strip and run 4 wires (3V3/GND/SDA/SCL) to the main board.
- Price: Adafruit 815 via DigiKey ≈ 130 kr (stock unverified) or clone ≈ 40-70 kr DK / 20 kr AliExpress; 4 x RGB LED ≈ 15-50 kr. Per scoreboard ≈ +110-250 kr.
CURRENTS (est., bench to confirm): sleep +~12 uA (≈ +0.25 mAh/day). Scan window, polled (field ~10 ms every 250 ms, ~30 mA during the field, soft PD between): ~1.5 mA avg. LEDs at typical brightness (1 colour each, ~2 mA) + PCA9685 awake: ~14 mA while lit.
BATTERY (scoreboard ≈ 9.0 mAh/day today at Medium sound, ~190 days):
- reader windows ~15 min/day: +0.4;
- LEDs lit 3 min/day: total ≈ 10.3 → ~5.4 months;
- 10 min/day: ≈ 11.9 → ~4.7 months;
- lit all through play (4.7 h): +66 → ~3 weeks. NOT viable.
=> 6 months holds only if the LEDs are feedback flashes (key press, scan OK = ~1 s), not a steady state. Needs a ux/firmware rule: LEDs off unless flashing / the check-in screen with a timeout.
READ RANGE: RC522 PCB antenna, ISO card ~3-5 cm in free air. PETG is RF-transparent: ~2-4 cm outside a 2 mm wall for cards, ~1-2 cm for key fobs. Mark a 'scan here' target.
MECHANICAL: module 40 x 60 mm, antenna loop ~35 x 40 at one end, flat against the inside of the wall behind the target, components facing in. Keep-outs from the loop:
- >= 10 mm from any metal/battery/ground plane behind or beside it;
- not over the e-paper panel (conductive layers) and >= 15 mm from the DESPI adapter;
- >= 20 mm from the buzzer (magnet);
- >= 20 mm from the XIAO;
- >= 50 mm from the 2 NTAG213 tags (otherwise the reader sees them; ferrite-in helps). Firmware should also ignore those two UIDs.
PCA9685 board 62 x 25 x ~10. Space in the 109 x 100 x 99 case is mechanical's call.
CONFLICTS:
1. All pins used, no growth left.
2. The SPI bus is shared: firmware serialises the e-paper and the reader; RC522 ≤ 10 MHz, mode 0.

## 2026-10-15 09:02  firmware -> lead
ack RC522 heads-up; I'll build once electronics' details land. Two points to settle first, so the rule works and fits the battery. (1) To be certain a fixed tag never joins, a scan has to count when the card LEAVES, if it was present ≤ 5 s, not when it is first seen. Otherwise the table's own NTAG joins once on every wake, before its 5 s are up. The same pattern as the keys (accept on release). Cost: the join shows ~1 poll (~0.2–0.3 s) after the card is pulled away, not on touch. If ux wants instant feedback, we could show 'reading…' on touch and add the player on release. Once a UID passes 5 s it stays ignored until it leaves. (2) Power: the RC522 has no low-power card detect. Finding a card means polling with the RF field on (~10–13 mA per burst), and a fixed tag in the field gets read on every poll. Polling every 250 ms during ACTIVE only, and soft power-down (~10 µA) otherwise, is roughly +0.3–0.5 mA while active. Electronics should put that in §3. No polling while the scoreboard sleeps, so a tap can't wake it; the keys or motion do. Questions for electronics' spec: SPI or I2C, which pins (the scoreboard has no free D pins; back pads GPIO4/5 are strapping pins, 6/7 are spoken for), an RST/power-down pin, and what a scan does on the API side (backend endpoint + openapi). I'll propose the openapi part once that's known.

## 2026-10-15 09:11  electronics -> firmware
Scoreboard reader + LEDs + VBUS (lead GO), drawn:
- RC522: MISO = GPIO4 (MTMS pad), CS = GPIO5 (MTDI pad); SCK/MOSI shared with the e-paper (D8/D10), ≤ 10 MHz, mode 0. RST is bridged to 3.3V at the module (no pin), IRQ unused. Soft power-down when not polling. Poll ONLY on scan-accepting screens (lead accepted).
- VBUS sense: GPIO6 (MTCK), HIGH on USB (2.8-3.1 V) → PIN_VBUS_SENSE = 6.
- PCA9685 @ 0x40 (All-Call 0x70) on the LIS3DH I2C bus. OE tied to GND.
- LEDs are COMMON CATHODE (changed from CA: 'off' and sleep are LOW with library defaults). Totem-pole (OUTDRV=1), INVRT=0, HIGH = on. LED n (1-4, n=1 above K1): R = ch 3(n-1), G = +1, B = +2. Through 220 ohm from 3V3: R max ~6 mA, G/B ~2 mA. Run ~1 mA per lit LED (lead accepted), ≤ 20 mA total. SLEEP the PCA9685 whenever nothing is lit.
ASSEMBLY S5 now promises these from scoreboard_bench; tell me if you'd word them differently:
(1) after the 3 sounds, light LED1 → LED4 red, green, blue in turn;
(2) log 'rfid uid <hex>' when a card is held on the reader;
(3) log 'usb: awake' when USB wakes it from sleep.
The troubleshooting table also refers to 'pca9685' and 'rfid' errors in the log at boot (chip not found / RC522 version register 0x00 or 0xFF).

## 2026-10-15 09:29  firmware -> electronics
Scan-in hardware is in firmware (builds; not run on hardware). Your ASSEMBLY S5 wording: (1) is implemented as written: after the 3 sounds, LED1→LED4 red, green, blue, 300 ms each. (2) Implemented as written: the bench build prints 'rfid uid <hex>' to serial while a card is held. It's serial only, never in the log ring or OTLP. (3) Please quote the real lines instead of 'usb: awake': a USB wake logs '[boot] usb', then '[usb] powered: staying awake (no sleep) for flashing'; unplugging logs '[usb] unplugged: sleeping as usual'. Boot errors for your troubleshooting table: 'pca9685: not found at 0x40', and 'rfid: RC522 version 0xNN', where 0x00 or 0xFF is followed by ' (not found: check MISO/CS/3V3)'. Genuine chips read 0x91/0x92. Implementation: SPI.begin(SCK 19, MISO 4, MOSI 18) shared with the e-paper, Arduino_MFRC522v2 at 4 MHz mode 0, CS GPIO5. Per poll: soft power-up, field on, 5 ms, REQA + select with a 2 ms answer window (lib default 25 ms), HaltA, field off, soft power-down. That's ~7 ms of field per poll, every 250 ms, only on scan screens. Near low_batt it skips a poll while a REST/OTLP request is in flight (your 480 mA note); the held long-poll is idle air time, so it doesn't block polls. PCA9685: MODE2 = OUTDRV (totem-pole), INVRT 0. LED n = ch 3n/3n+1/3n+2. All dark → ALL_LED_OFF then SLEEP. LED_PALETTE in include/scoreboard/board.h starts at R 700/4095 (~1 mA), G/B 2048 (~1 mA), with mixes for yellow/cyan/magenta/white. Bench tunes it.

## 2026-10-15 09:30  firmware -> electronics
Confirmed: the production build reacts visibly on the Lobby. At TOUCH, with no server involved, all four key LEDs flash white for 0.15 s and it blips (C7, 50 ms; silent if the table's sound_volume is 0). On RELEASE (≤ 5 s) it sends the scan, and the strip shows the result for 3 s: '✓  <name> joined' + 2 blinks in that player's colour, '<name> is already in', the link QR for an unknown badge, 'Full. Remove a player first.', and so on. Suggested S6 wording: 'Wake the board onto an EMPTY Lobby (no players, so no steady LEDs) with sound on. For 10 s, touch nothing: there must be no white flash and no blip. Then tap a badge: white flash + blip at touch.' What a failure means: a flash/blip with no card present = a fixed tag (the side NTAG) is inside the reader's range. Firmware then ignores it after 5 s, so it never joins, but it would still flash and blip once on every wake, so fix the placement or shielding. Note the reader only listens on Lobby/Teams/Remove-who and the first 60 s of Finished; on Live it is off by design.

- Battery: if board 2 only wakes for animations/flashes (steady Lobby/Teams stays on the 4 key LEDs = today), ≈ 5.0-5.1 months. If all 10 are steady for ux's 10 min/day: +~1.3-2 mAh/day → ≈ 4.3-4.6 months.
- Build: moderate. +~45 joints, 18 colour wires + GND bus, ~1 h, same steps as today.
- Effects: per-LED colour at 12-bit (smooth fades), chase/sweep across 10 points, per-player colour in 2 zones, coarse gradient.
(b) Addressable strip (SK6812/WS2812, 8-16 px) + 5 V boost + switch + level shift.
- Freeing a pin: VBUS on the key ladder FAILS. It can't both wake (needs < 0.83 V) and stay clear of the K4 window, and the keys misread while USB is in. CS/buzzer/RST sharing corrupts the strip or resets the e-paper. The only workable data pin is EPD DC (D7: the panel ignores DC while its CS is high) gated through a 74HCT08 AND (also the 3.3→5 V level shifter) enabled by PCA ch 15, sent by firmware with RMT.
- Power: the boost (e.g. Pololu U1V11F5) passes VIN through when disabled, so it ALSO needs a P-FET load switch on PCA ch 14. The strip draws ~1 mA/px even 'black'.
- Parts ≈ 130-150 kr.
- Lit: 16 px ≈ 16 mA idle + LEDs, at 5 V via the boost ≈ 50 mA from the pack → 10 min/day ≈ +8 mAh/day → ≈ 3 months. 8 px ≈ 3.9 months.
- Build: hard-ish (boost, switch, logic chip, D7 sharing in firmware).
- Effects: best (smooth gradients, rainbow, fine chase).
- Fails the 5-month target unless lit time drops to ~3 min/day.
(c) Cheapest: use board 1's 4 spare channels. One more RGB on ch 12-14 + one single-colour (white) LED on ch 15, or 4 single-colour accent LEDs.
- ≈ 15-20 kr, 0 pins, ~6 wires, battery unchanged (board 1 is awake anyway).
- Effects: a simple 5-6 point chase/sweep and white accents; per-player colour still only on the RGB ones.
RECOMMEND (a) with the firmware rule 'board 2 = animations and flashes only'. It meets ~5 months, costs ≈ 165 kr, needs no new pins and no new circuit type, and gives the user real 'fancier' effects (10 RGB under the diffuser). (b) is fanciest but ~3 months and the most fragile; (c) if the user only wants a bit more sparkle cheaply. The PCA9685 awake-current bench item decides how much margin (a) has (6 mA datasheet vs maybe ~3).
Open for mechanical: the 10 LED positions under the diffuser (e.g. 4 above the keys + 6 between/outside, or an even ~9 mm pitch).

## 2026-10-15 10:49  firmware -> electronics
Done, plus one thing you didn't ask for. (1) The reader skips a poll while EPD BUSY is HIGH (SSD1683: HIGH = busy). A skipped poll doesn't count as 'card removed', so a card held across a refresh doesn't join early. Today GxEPD2 refreshes block the same thread anyway, so this is belt and braces. (2) The real gap: GxEPD2's partial update (0x22/0xFC) leaves the panel's analog ON afterwards (BUSY low, _power_is_on = true), so the DESPI-C02 boost could keep running between refreshes while the field is on. I now call powerOff() after every refresh. The boost only runs during the refresh itself, idle current drops, and each refresh is ~0.1 s slower (power-up). Bench item added: partial refreshes must still not flash after the power-off.

GxEPD2 leaves the panel's analog/boost ON after partial refreshes, so it could switch next to the field between refreshes. Also, while the reader listens, full refreshes are postponed (partials only), so the Lobby only does a full refresh on cold boot. ## 2026-10-15 11:15  firmware -> lead
QUESTION: (for you/mechanical) on the 3-ball drawer queue. The confirmations are YES; one case loses a goal. (1) Ball resting in the beam: counted once at 5 ms, 'stuck' after 10 s, never re-counted. After it clears, the next goal counts normally once lockout_ms (1.5 s) has passed since the clear. Goals are seconds apart, so that's fine. (2) Two touching balls through the beam = ONE count. At beam height the gap between two touching balls is ~0.1 mm vs a 3 mm aperture, so the beam can't separate them. That's right when one of them was already counted (a waiting ball nudged back through), but WRONG if both are goals. Example: a ball stalls just upstream of the beam (not counted yet), the next goal ball hits it, and they pass together → 1 count for 2 goals. (3) Related: a ball entering the beam < 1.5 s after the previous one cleared is treated as a roll-back and ignored. E.g. ball 2 creeps through right after ball 1 is pushed out. Firmware can't tell these from bounces, because the beam alone has no direction or ball count. So the mechanical requirement is: a ball must never stop UPSTREAM of the beam (or in it); queue only downstream. My question: can mechanical confirm that? If not, the lever is lockout_ms (server config, bench-calibrated against real bounce-backs). Tests pin (1)-(3) (test_detector_queue_cases, native 77/77).

## 2026-10-15 11:19  electronics -> lead
Feasibility: mechanical keyboard switches instead of the B3F. Short answer: YES, easy electrically.
1. Ladder: NO change. MX and Choc are plain 2-pin SPST like the B3F (which used 2 diagonal legs). K1 direct, K2 4.7k, K3 10k, K4 22k to the GND bus, 100k pull-up on the main board. Gold-crosspoint contacts are fine at the ladder's ~33 uA.
2. Wiring: recommend HAND-WIRED, no perfboard for the keys.
   - The switches clip into a printed plate (MX cutout 14.0 x 14.0, 1.5 mm plate; Choc 13.8 x 13.8, 1.2-1.3 mm). Pins are wired like a hand-wired keyboard: KEYS bus to one pin of each switch, ladder resistors soldered straight from the other pin to a GND bus wire. The same 2 wires go to J_KEY.
   - On perfboard, MX's pin 2 (+2.54, +5.08) is on the grid but pin 1 (−3.81, +2.54) is half a pitch off, and the Ø4 centre post needs drilling. Choc is metric, all off-grid.
   - The key strip then only carries the 4 LEDs, unless mechanical prefers LEDs in the plate.
   - Mechanical's call: MX is ~11.6 mm above the plate + cap (deeper case); Choc ~5 mm + cap (closest to today).
3. Debounce: firmware has KEY_DEBOUNCE_MS = 30. MX/Choc bounce ≤ 5 ms (Cherry spec), B3F similar, so no firmware change. The press is lighter (MX ~45-60 cN, Choc ~50 cN vs B3F 255 gf); table shake won't press a key.
4. Hot-swap: possible but not recommended. Kailh hot-swap sockets (MX CPG151101S11, Choc CPG135001S30) are SMD parts made for PCB pads. Hand-wired, they'd need a printed holder + wires soldered to their tabs, ~1-2 kr each. Low value: nobody swaps switches on a scoreboard.
5. Parts if they don't own enough (4 + 1 spare per scoreboard): MX-style (Gateron/Outemu/Kailh) ~3-5 kr each, a 10-35 pack ≈ 40-100 kr (AliExpress 1-3 wk; DK keyboard shops faster). Choc v1 ~6-8 kr each, 10-pack ≈ 60-80 kr. Keycaps: printed by mechanical (free) or blank packs ≈ 30-60 kr. Net vs the B3F (4 x ~5 kr): ≈ +10-30 kr per scoreboard with printed caps. The 4 ladder resistors + J_KEY are unchanged.

## 2026-10-15 11:21  mechanical -> lead
Feasibility: mechanical keyboard switches for the 4 keys (estimates +/-2 mm, not built). The constraint that matters: ux fixes caps at 2 mm proud. Keyboard switches stand tall, so they must sit RECESSED in a well behind the face with their own printed plate. Upside: the plate takes the press, so the backer bar and its 4 mm insertion travel go away. That's what lowers the case. Today's key stack reaches ~31 mm behind the face; each mm less is ~0.7 mm off H and ~0.7 off depth at 46 deg.
(a) MX (14x14 cutouts, 1.5 plate): cap top ~15 above the plate, so the plate sits ~13 behind the face and the switch PCB/wiring ~20-23 behind. Stack ~23 instead of ~31: H ~95 (-5.5), depth ~142 (-6). LED bar: LEDs on a strip at the switches' PCB level end ~8 behind the bar, so today's bar + baffles work unchanged.
(b) Kailh Choc v1 (13.8x13.8, 1.2 plate): cap top ~8 above the plate, so the plate sits ~6 behind the face; stack ~12. H ~89 (-11), depth ~137 (-11). Best height, but the 5 mm through-hole LEDs no longer fit: on a strip that shallow the dome would stick out past the face. The bar needs SMD RGB LEDs on a deeper separate LED board, or a different LED mount: electronics work.
Plate/key row: a separate printed plate (MX 1.5 / Choc 1.2 thick) on posts behind the face, switches clipped in, hand-wired (the MX and Choc pins aren't on the 2.54 perfboard grid, so no key strip for the switches; a small strip remains for the LEDs). 20.32 pitch is fine on a plate. Cap wells in the face, 2 mm proud.
Caps: ux needs >= 4 mm between caps, so 16x11 caps at 20.32 pitch. Bought caps don't fit that: MX caps are 18 wide (2.3 gaps), Choc caps 17.5. So PRINTED caps with the stem: Choc's 2-prong stem prints well in PETG; the MX cross stem works but needs tolerance tuning (test-print a few). Bought caps would need ux to accept ~2.3 mm gaps or a wider pitch (that breaks the label grid).
Feel: MX 4 mm travel / Choc 3 mm, ~0.5 N, vs the tact switch's 0.25 mm / 2.55 N. Much nicer to press; the tape still sees the user's jab force.
Recommendation: if the user wants them, Choc gives the lowest case (~89 H) but needs an LED rework with electronics. MX is a drop-in for the LED bar at ~95 H. Which switches does the user have?

## 2026-10-15 11:39  ux -> mechanical
MX keys (user): UX rules updated in ux/PHYSICAL-UX.md Keys. The important one: ACTUATION POINT vs HEIGHT. A fingertip is wider than the 16x11 cap and the face stops it at flush, so the switch must actuate >= 0.5 mm before the cap is flush. With caps 2 mm proud that means a speed switch (~1.1-1.2 mm actuation). A standard 2.0 mm actuation needs caps >= 2.5 mm proud (edge r >= 0.8). Also: force >= 0.6 N (0.8 preferred, heavier than the usual 45 gf); cap side play <= 0.3 mm at the top (no rattle on a shaking table); >= 0.5 mm clearance to the face opening on all sides (no rubbing or sticking); every cap corner must actuate. Tactile or clicky preferred, linear OK. Please send the MX key row (cap centres, the active-area-to-cap gap, cap height) and I'll check the label/key alignment.

## 2026-10-15 11:39  ux -> lead
progress: MX keys checked in PHYSICAL-UX. Fix: a speed switch (~1.2 mm actuation), or caps >= 2.5 mm proud. Also: force >= 0.6 N (resting hands, table knocks), cap play <= 0.3 mm (no rattle), >= 0.5 mm clearance to the opening, every corner actuates. Tactile/clicky preferred, linear OK (the key LED flash gives instant feedback). The label/key alignment check waits for mechanical's MX key row.

## 2026-10-15 14:02  firmware -> mechanical
firmware: agree, no change. min_block_ms stays 5 (its margin is 4x at 20 ms; I won't go above 10). The beam moving to s 200-215 is fine for the detector: a rebound that reaches the beam does so within lockout_ms 1.5 s, so it is ignored and pushes the re-arm out, as before. The one hard limit is unchanged: a ball resting IN the beam. Counting from the 36 mm ball, beam at 200 means 5 queued balls (to ~180 mm) still clear it, but a 6th sits in the beam. From then on every goal is missed (the incoming ball touches it, so the beam never clears) until someone empties the drawer. So keep 'room for N balls before the beam' in the drawer spec, measured from the final beam position.

## 2026-10-15 14:14  electronics -> lead
done: (1) Scoreboard listen interval 1 while a match is live. The extra cost is the 2 extra beacon wakes per 307 ms. Espressif's test AP gives about +0.6 mA; with my real-AP factor (x2.5, same as the DTIM3 budget) it is +1.8 mA. I budget +1.8 mA. Split: ACTIVE 4.7 h = live match up to 4 h (all of lead's play time, worst case) + ~0.7 h of idle tails and lobby. Live: 1.5 -> 3.3 mA = 13.2 mAh. Rest: 1.5 mA = 1.1 mAh. Total 11.2 -> 18.4 mAh/day, so about 92 days = 3.0 months at Medium (2.9 at High). If the AP behaves like Espressif's: about 13.6 mAh/day = 4.1 months. The 1-month target (57 mAh/day) still has about 3x margin. What it buys: buffered frames wait about 51 ms on average (102 worst) instead of about 154 (307), so about 0.1 s faster on average and 0.2 s worst case. README budget is updated. Two things for firmware. In ESP-IDF, listen_interval only applies in WIFI_PS_MAX_MODEM and is sent at association, so check that it takes effect without a reconnect. The alternative is esp_wifi_set_ps(MIN_MODEM) while a match is live (wakes every DTIM, which equals LI1 on DTIM-1 APs). Stale '≈ 5 months (4.7 at High)' text needs updating in ux/SCOREBOARD-UI.md lines 216 and 458 and in video's 'about five months' line: please route the new '≈ 3 months' to ux and video. (2) Full-width IR beam, about 115 mm (131 mm optical path with the same 8 mm aperture recesses vs 56 mm now): yes, it works. Light falls as 1/d², so the signal is 5.5x weaker. With the TSAL6200 at today's 1 mA, typ I_c is about 13 uA, which is only 1.2x the 11 uA needed for a clean LOW at 220k. Option A, keep the TSAL6200: R_LED 390R (5.5 mA) restores today's 6.5x typical margin. Goal counter +21 mAh/day -> about 32 mAh/day, about 1.7 months. Option B (recommended): swap to the TSAL6100. It has the same 5 mm package and pinout, ±10° instead of ±17°, and 170 mW/sr typ / 80 min at 100 mA vs 72/40 for the TSAL6200 (Vishay datasheet), so about 2.4x on axis. R_LED 1k (2.2 mA, an existing calibration step) gives 6.3x typical margin. Goal counter +5.6 mAh/day -> about 16.6 mAh/day, about 3.4 months. Use 680R (3.2 mA) if the bench wants worst-case parity, about 2.6 months. Keep R_PU at 220k: 470k would slow the edges towards min_block_ms. Same price, about 0.5 USD. Mechanical notes: the narrower LED needs the two bores aligned within about ±5°, and printed bores do that. Keep the walls and floor near the beam matte and dark. Optional deeper apertures (Ø3 x 15 mm) keep the emitter's cone off the floor at the far wall (spot ±13 mm vs the 17 mm beam height) and cost about 20 % of the signal. (2) Estimate, beam to sound, warm connections: typical ~140 ms (was ~240 ms), worst ~450 ms. Steps: counted 6, NVS 3, lane+TLS 8, uplink 4, office to server 15, server 30, server to AP 15, AP holds until the next beacon 50 avg / 102 max, scoreboard parse + sound 10. But the ball needs ~0.3-0.5 s from the mouth to the beam at 240 mm (mechanical), so mouth to sound is ~0.45-0.65 s typical: the 0.5 s target is met only at the low end, and the beam position is the biggest lever. Tail: after a quiet spell longer than the server's keep-alive idle timeout (Kestrel default 130 s), the goal counter must reconnect (TCP + TLS, each reply held by its listen interval 3): +0.5-1.2 s. Needs a reserve/persist split and the REST lane above the app task's priority; I'll do it if the bench shows NVS > 10 ms. (c) Starting the sound before the full parse: -2-5 ms, not worth it; the sound already starts before the e-paper redraw. (3) Bench plan: README 'Goal -> sound latency': 30 goals at 20/60/150/300 s gaps from NTP epoch log times (the mock now prints each record's device time), with and without a live match, 240 fps video with audio as ground truth, PPK2 wake spacing 102 vs 307 ms. ## 2026-10-15 14:28  backend -> lead
QUESTION: occupancy + per-table stats, proposal (I build after analytics' spec + your OK).
PRESENCE SIGNALS THE SERVER ALREADY HAS (no new device traffic):
1. Game state (history kept): table_matches started_at / last_activity_at / ended_at / status / score, and table_goals received_at (+ device occurred_at). Strongest: a live match with a goal = in use.
2. Lobby: roster entries created_at (players scanned in, teams made at 0:0) = in use, people at the table. Cleared after 30 min idle.
3. Scoreboard awake: it long-polls every <=25 s while awake and sleeps after idle_timeout_s (default 300; server doesn't override it) with no button press. Each request sets devices.last_seen_at, so last_seen_at < ~60 s ago = board awake = someone touched it in the last ~5 min. There's no in-memory waiter registry, and none needed.
4. Goal counter awake: it pulls config once per wake (wake = table movement or a goal) -> last_seen_at. Afterwards it is silent until goals or its sleep status.
5. Status reason=sleep: sent idle_timeout_s after the last goal or movement; uptime_ms = wake length. So a wake session is [sleep_at - uptime_ms, sleep_at - idle_timeout_s] = real use incl. unscored play. Caveat: only the LAST status body is stored (devices.last_status), no history.
6. Heartbeat (timer wake, <=24 h): a status only, no config pull, so last_seen_at ~= last_status_at with reason heartbeat. Excluded as not use.
Not available: anything during sleep; per-request history of polls.
PROPOSED API:
(a) occupancy on TableResponse, so it's in GET .../tables, .../tables/{id}/live and admin tables with no extra calls: { status: free|in_use|just_finished, since: ISO|null, confidence: high|medium|low, reason: game|lobby|devices_awake|null }. in_use+high = live match with a goal, or a lobby with players (since = first goal or first scan); in_use+medium = only devices awake (board polling, or a goal counter woken after its last sleep status; since = first wake seen); just_finished = a match ended < N min ago (since = ended_at); free = otherwise. confidence low = free but devices are offline > 36 h (we can't see). N and windows come from analytics.
(b) GET /organizations/{orgId}/tables/{tableId}/stats?from&to&tz=<IANA> -> ready-made numbers per analytics' metrics: each { value, n, min_n, enough }, the heatmap as a 7x24 count grid in tz, and the tz echoed. There's NO org time zone in the model today; I propose a tz query param (the viewer's browser zone, default UTC) instead of a new org setting. Say if you'd rather have an org setting.
(c) GET /organizations/{orgId}/tables/stats?from&to&tz -> one row per table: occupancy + headline numbers (games, utilisation, avg length) for the overview.
(d) Storage: stats come from matches + goals (history exists). If analytics wants utilisation incl. unscored play, I'd add a small table_wake_sessions row per sleep status (start/end from uptime_ms/idle_timeout; still no new traffic). One extra table + migration.
Auth: same as the existing table reads (org members); stats are read-only. Questions: (1) OK with tz as a query param? (2) OK to add wake-session rows if analytics needs them?

## 2026-10-15 14:36  electronics -> lead
QUESTION: premium sound proposal. Approve it, and I'll draw it, update the BOM/ASSEMBLY and order the bench A/B parts. Full write-up: electronics/premium-sound.md. Summary: GPIO7 (MTDO) becomes a 1-bit PDM DAC. The C6's I2S0 PDM TX has a hardware PCM-to-PDM converter, and its ONE_LINE_DAC mode needs no clock pin. DMA feeds it 16-bit samples at 22.05 kHz, up-sampled 128x to a 2.8 MHz bitstream, so there's no per-sample CPU work. Fallbacks: LEDC 10-bit or SDM 8-bit. Signal path: GPIO7 -> 1k/10nF -> 10k/1nF (2 poles near 16 kHz) -> Adafruit 2130 PAM8302 A+ (A- to GND). The amp is fed from the pack BEFORE D1, with 470 uF at the amp, so its 0.3 A peaks don't sag the XIAO rail. Speaker: PUI AS04008PO-2-LW152-R, 40x28.3x12 mm, 8 ohm 1 W. SD comes from PCA9685 ch15 (HIGH = on; the PCA powers up with every channel off, so the amp defaults to silent). The amp board's SD pull-up resistor MUST be removed: it costs 0.5 mA = 12 mAh/day. Without it, standby is <=1 uA. Removed parts: buzzer, BC337, R_B, R_BD, D3, R_SND socket. Net about +70 kr per scoreboard (695 -> ~765). DigiKey had the 2130 at about 32 kr but 0 in stock; a DK/EU Adafruit reseller is needed for speed. Speaker: DigiKey, ~51 kr, in stock. Quality: noise is set by ripple on the 3.3 V rail (~60-70 dB SNR), and there may be a faint Wi-Fi beacon tick in chime tails (bench item). The speaker covers about 450 Hz-10 kHz, so no bass: good for chimes and bells. Loudness at 1 m: peaks of ~76-78 dB SPL on High, vs 67-72 dBA for the buzzer. Medium is about today's High. Current while playing: ~40 mA at Medium, ~70 mA at High, ~300 mA peaks (the C6 can't light-sleep during I2S, plus the PCA awake, plus the amp). At ~230 sounds/day of ~1 s: Medium 2.6 mAh/day (buzzer 0.4) -> scoreboard 20.6 mAh/day, about 2.7 months; High about 2.5 months. Mechanical: speaker footprint 40x28.3, <=15 mm deep incl. wires. Mount it behind a wall grille (30-40% open) facing the players, rim sealed with a 1 mm foam ring. Back volume >= 20 cm3 (the closed case is fine). Magnet/frame >=25 mm from the RC522 loop copper and never over or under it; >=15 mm from the XIAO antenna; >=20 mm from the NTAG. Amp board (~23x18 mm) >=30 mm from the loop; speaker leads twisted, <=15 cm. ux's sounds v2 fits: 40 mm in a sealed back is ~3-6 dB down at 600-700 Hz, not >10, so no transposition. Volume is a digital gain (Low -18 / Med -9 / High 0, trim pot = bench max); 154 KiB of samples is fine. ux asked whether the speaker could go on the existing BC337: only as a toy. It would carry ~0.2 A of DC at silence (unipolar), get half the swing, and the BC337 is too slow for a 78 kHz carrier. So it's amp or nothing. I recommend a bench A/B before the user decides: A = today's buzzer, B = amp + speaker on a breadboard, same firmware and ux's WAVs (optional C = speaker on the BC337 to hear why not).

(3) Windows: every stat uses the request's [from, to) (default the last 30 days) rather than its own fixed window (TS2 8 weeks, TS4 12 weeks). The page passes a longer from for those, and minN/enough follow your table, the heatmap also needing >= 4 weeks of data. (4) TS3/game winning score: the table's default league's, even for linked games in another league. (5) TS6 alert and TS1 trend arrows: not computed (observability / UI); averageGamesPerWeek over the full weeks is the trend base. (6) Fast gaps = consecutive counted goals from the same counter in one match under 3 s. Docs: api/docs/hardware-api.md 'Occupancy and stats'.

## 2026-10-15 15:39  firmware -> lead
firmware on LIS3DH vs a spring switch on D1 (facts). WHAT THE LIS3DH DOES TODAY, both devices, nothing else: (1) deep-sleep wake (ext1 on D1, wake cause 'motion'); (2) staying awake: every 2 s (MOTION_POLL_MS) the app reads the latched INT1 over I2C, and any motion since the last read counts as activity and restarts the 300 s idle timer; (3) sleep guards: the latch is cleared before deep sleep, and if INT1 is still active the device takes a timer wake instead of a wake loop; in battery cutoff a motion wake only re-measures the pack. No tilt, tamper, orientation or acceleration data is used anywhere; 64 mg threshold, 10 Hz. Other activity sources stay as they are: goals, keys, scans, server changes. WITH A SWITCH: the core doesn't change, because it only calls Hal::motionSeen() every 2 s. HAL: an edge ISR on D1 sets a 'pulse seen' flag and disarms itself (no wake storm in light sleep); motionSeen() returns and clears it and re-arms. 'N pulses in T s' becomes 'pulses in >= K of the last M 2-s windows' (knobs MOTION_MIN_WINDOWS, default 1 = as today), plus a 5 ms debounce. Own sounds: on the scoreboard the HAL ignores pulses while the buzzer/speaker plays + 100 ms (it knows). Keys and goals needn't be masked, they are activity anyway. Deep-sleep wake: ext1 level wake on D1. A contact burst must hold the level for roughly >= 100 us to be caught; if the switch's closures are shorter, electronics should add an RC stretcher (bench item). A switch resting closed is covered by the existing timer-wake fallback. Note: the scoreboard keeps I2C for the PCA9685, while the goal device would drop I2C entirely (D4/D5 freed). EFFORT: about half a day as a build flag MOTION_HW = LIS3DH | SWITCH (both kept, like SOUND_HW): ISR, ext1 polarity, mask while sounding, board.h knobs, README/FLASHING notes, then bench tuning of the sensitivity (play wakes it, a passer-by doesn't).

## 2026-10-15 15:41  electronics -> lead
done: motion-wake assessment, electronics/motion-wake-options.md. RECOMMEND: a bare spring vibration switch (SW-18010P class, not the SW-420 module) on D1 for both devices, under 3 conditions. (a) An RC stretch: 3V3 -> SW (in a 2-pin socket) -> 1k -> D1, with 100nF + 1M to GND. A ≥0.5 ms touch holds D1 HIGH ~29 ms and bounce merges into one pulse, so ext1 ANY_HIGH (same pin and polarity as INT1) can't miss it. 0 uA when open, 3.3 uA if it rests closed (firmware must then sleep on a 10-min timer, not wake-loop). (b) A firmware wake gate: on a touch, power the beam and stay in light sleep without Wi-Fi; join only after ≥3 bursts ≥200 ms apart within 10 s. A rejected bump costs ~0.006 mAh vs ~0.3 mAh for an ungated false wake. With the gate the battery is unchanged (+0.05 mAh/day); without it, 20 bumps/day = -35 % life. Goals during the gate are counted and queued, never lost. (c) The socket, because of WEAR (main risk): LCSC rates it at 1 M operations, and heavy play may reach that in ~2-3 months. Bench logs touches per day; it's a 1 kr swap at a battery change. (1) Reliability: ball hits, rod slams and drawer landings fire it; leaning and slow spins mostly don't, but a served ball gives impacts within seconds. Walk-past bumps, cups and door slams are single bursts, which the gate rejects. Grade: sellers disagree on the suffix, so buy a mixed 10P/15P/20P pack and bench-pick. Expect 18010P in the goal counter (damped drawer) and 10P or 15P/20P on the scoreboard (taped to the top). Orientation: axis vertical. ## 2026-10-15 19:17  ux -> lead
done: protective window. Recommendation: a LOW-HAZE ANTI-GLARE (satin) hard-coated PC, textured side out. A glossy window mirrors ~5-10% of the light at players' angles, and e-paper has no light of its own, so a ceiling light or window would sit on the score for someone. Strong matte over an air gap blurs and goes milky; satin blurs < 1 pixel. Glossy is an acceptable fallback: at 50° the over-table lamp's reflection lands 2.6-4 m out, past the table end. Gap: target 0.5 mm, MAX 1.0 mm (the image then sits ≤ 2.3 mm under the surface, 'under glass', not sunk). It must be more than the shot deflection + 0.3 mm; if not, go to 3 mm PC rather than more air. Parallax: oversize the opening ≥2 mm top/bottom and ≥5 mm left/right, or print a black border on the window's back. Image ~20% dimmer, still fine. Bench: a satin and a glossy sample over the printed mockup at 50° in the real room. Told mechanical + electronics. File: ux/PHYSICAL-UX.md 'Protective window'.

## 2026-10-15 19:19  mechanical -> lead
QUESTION: v5, two problems that need a decision. I'm building everything else meanwhile.
(1) PROTECTIVE WINDOW vs ux's <= 1 mm air gap. My estimate for a ball at ~5 m/s (a shot that leaves the table) on a ~95 x 72 PC window, between the plate's effective-mass bound and the static-energy bound:
  - 2 mm PC: 1.5-4 mm deflection.
  - 3 mm PC: 1-2.2 mm.
  - At 10 m/s, double that.
So with <= 1 mm of air the window WILL touch the panel on a hard hit. 'No load path to the panel' then needs > 4 mm of air, which ux rejects (the image looks sunk). Proposal:
  - 3 mm low-haze anti-glare PC, rebated flush from the front, ~0.8 mm gap.
  - Its border rests on a 2 mm ledge OUTSIDE the panel's glass outline.
  - The e-paper panel gets a FULL-AREA backing (the retainer frame becomes a plate, with 1 mm foam behind the panel). If the window touches, the panel is pressed flat onto support (compression, no bending), which glass tolerates.
  - The alternative is 'touch is allowed, with no backing', which risks cracking the panel. OK to go with the backing?
(2) USB-C ACCESS: the main board's port faces the INNER wall, 16 mm from the bead counter's end cube. A straight plug (overmould ~12 x 7, 20-25 long) would overlap the counter's bead row by ~4 mm. Options:
  (a) Right-angle USB-C cable only (the plug turns along the wall): no design change, but a special cable.
  (b) Panel-mount USB-C in the BACK cover via a short C-C M-F extension (CC must pass through; electronics picks it). It's reachable over the rail's outer edge.
  (c) Port through the OUTER wall: it's accessible over the flush side panel, but the board would have to move into the wing, where the speaker and reader already are.
  I recommend (b).
Also FYI, decided within your brief:
  - Side panel: ~flush with the rail top (photos 12/13), so there's no wall above the rail, and the right end is the 170 free one.
  - Speaker: on the outer wall back-low. The face below the badge can't hold 25 mm from the loop at 92 deep. It needs the loop at the TOP of the wing and LED5 BELOW the RC522 module (the insert's tongue runs down to it): ~25-26 mm on paper, which electronics will check.
  - Option B buzzer: a disc in the same outer-wall grille.
  - MIRROR: the board cradle can't simply be mirrored (a real board can't be mirrored), so the mirrored build needs its own internal pass. I'll do it after the right-end build passes, unless you say otherwise.
  - LED bar: 2 mm opal ACRYLIC behind a 0.5 lip can crack on a hit. Suggest 2 mm opal POLYCARBONATE (same hand cut). Keys and the PETG badge insert are fine.

v5 back-cover USB-C (lead's decision): a generic 'USB 3.1 Type-C male to female panel-mount extension with screw holes', full-featured (passes CC), 20-30 cm, AliExpress (bom S25). Typical dimensions, *est.*, to measure on arrival: flange plate ~26-28 x 8-9 x 2 mm with 2 holes ~Ø3 at 17 mm centres (screws M2.5/M3 are usually included); socket opening ~9 x 3.5 mm, so the panel cutout is ~9.5 x 4 mm (rounded); behind the flange a moulded body ~12 x 7 x 15 mm, then a Ø4-5 mm cable. The male end's overmould is ~12 x 6.5 x 20-25 mm and plugs straight into the XIAO's USB-C, so it needs ~25 mm straight clearance in front of the port, then a ≥15 mm bend radius; coil the excess away from the RC522 loop and never across it. Mounting: 2 screws into printed bosses (or heat-set inserts) from inside, or a printed clip that traps the flange. Either is fine electrically. Please also send me the v5 distances for the speaker on its outer wall and LED5 below the RC522, and I'll check them against the keep-out list (speaker ≥25 mm from the loop copper, never over or under it; LED5 beside it ≥ ~10 mm, wires leading away).

## 2026-10-15 20:20  electronics -> mechanical
TEFT4300 in R's pod. Fit checked against your numbers (bore Ø3.2 for a Ø3.0 ±0.1 body, flange seat 3.5 behind the tip, tip 4 behind a Ø3 aperture, all as dimensions.md). Answers:
1. 4.5 mm behind the flange: enough for the SEATED part, not for INSERTING it. Seated: the legs bend ≥ 2 mm behind the flange (Vishay practice; pliers between the body and the bend), 0.45 legs with a tight radius, so ~3 mm in total; 4.5 fits. But going in from the open bottom, the body must slide 3.5 mm along its axis into the bore, so with the legs already bent it needs ~3.5 + 3 ≈ 7 mm behind the seated flange. ACTION, either (a) ≥ 7 mm behind the seated flange, or (b) make the body bore a drop-in CRADLE: a U-slot Ø3.2 open downward to the pod's open bottom (plus a matching slot for the Ø3.9 flange), so it drops in already seated and a hot-glue dot holds it. Keep the 4 mm Ø3 tube in front of the tip a CLOSED hole for light shielding. (b) keeps your 4.5; I'd take (b). Please add an assert for whichever.
2. Joints: green/black wires soldered to the legs after the bend (legs cut to ~8 mm), heat-shrunk, ~Ø2 x 10 mm each, lying in the 16 mm vertical run along the skin. Please leave ~2.5 mm of free thickness there.
3. Wire and length: two 26 AWG Dupont-jumper wires (~Ø1.3-1.5 each) side by side in your 3.5 x 3 U-channel: fits; untwisted inside the channel. One whole 30 cm jumper per wire (ASSEMBLY section 4, as now): ~170 mm to R's front end (16 + 150), leaving ~120 mm onward to the board's J_PT. If J_PT on the sled board is further than ~100 mm from R's front end, tell me.
4. Plug: no JST. The existing female Dupont plug (one 2-pin 2.54 housing, ~5.1 x 2.5 x 14 mm) pushes onto the board's 2-pin J_PT header, and that IS the disconnect. JST-PH stays for the battery only (it's polarised; this one deliberately isn't, see 5).
5. Polarity: the TEFT4300's C/E marking is easy to misread, so it's bench-checked (ASSEMBLY section 6: beam lit = LOW, blocked = HIGH). If it's wrong, the 2-pin plug is turned round. So no polarity mark is needed on the part. Mark the plug 'SENSOR' with a tape flag.
ASSEMBLY section 4 step 3 updated with the bend, cut and slim-joint steps.

## 2026-10-16 09:53  firmware -> electronics
ACTION (beam health, joint proposal): firmware's part is in firmware/beam-health-firmware-2026-10-16.md (health check, states, reporting, server config, cost, recommendation). Please merge or link it into electronics/beam-health-2026-10-16.md; the circuit is yours. Key point: with R_PU 220k the lit node is saturated (about 14 uA), so an ADC on the node with the LED at full shows no margin. Firmware needs (1) the LED on its own GPIO with R_PU staying on D3, so LED-off ambient reads keep the pull-up; (2) a weak test drive (2nd resistor, own GPIO, about 1/5 current) for a graded margin; (3) an ADC pin on the receiver node in parallel with D8: back pad GPIO4-6, or D2 if VBUS sense moves to back pad GPIO6 like the scoreboard. ## 2026-10-16 11:26  analytics -> electronics
analytics re shot speed: it's fun only (like own goals), never in contribution/MVP/rating. Best uses: "fastest goal" on the finished screen, hardest goal of the week, and each player's best and median. It counts goals only (misses aren't seen) and needs a known scorer (G1).
Relative ranking is enough, but players will compare km/h across tables, so show "≈ 34 km/h" with a per-table calibration knob, or else a 0-100 scale with no unit.
Accuracy: a per-player median over ≥ 10 goals is fine at ±20 % random error. A single-shot record (hardest of the week) needs about ±10 %, because the max picks out the biggest positive errors. A bias between tables must be < 10 % if tables are compared.
Force-only (depends on where the ball hits): OK as a relative "shot power" median, not for records. Hit-position noise lands on the single max, and players who aim at different spots get a bias the median doesn't remove.

## 2026-10-16 11:26  firmware -> electronics
answers (all EST, nothing built): (1) While the table is in use the counter is in auto light sleep, not deep sleep, so yes: set the LIS3DH to 5.376 kHz low-power (or 1.344 kHz), +/-16 g, AOI threshold on INT1, FIFO in trigger mode (32 samples = 6 ms at 5.4 kHz, so the samples around the hit are kept). Wake on INT1, read the FIFO over I2C (~3 ms), take peak g. About 185 uA while active, so about +0.9 mAh/day; back to 10 Hz for deep sleep. The board in the drawer is far from the hit, so a 2nd LIS3DH at 0x18 on the back panel is better. Peak g only gives speed after calibration, and at 5 kHz a ~1 ms impact gets ~5 samples (underestimates).
(2) A piezo into the ADC with the CPU awake: continuous ADC needs a PM lock, so about 15-25 mA over 4.7 h = 70-115 mAh/day, i.e. weeks instead of months. Not viable. Use a peak-hold (diode + RC) plus a comparator into a GPIO to wake, then read the held peak once: about 0 cost.
(3) Two beams: the first edge wakes the CPU from light sleep, ~0.3-1 ms late with jitter. Then hold a PM lock for ~150 ms, so the later edges are timed to the microsecond (esp_timer in the ISR). So time the two beams' CLEAR edges (or beam 2 enter vs exit), not beam 1's wake edge. The real limit is the receiver edge time (up to 2 ms at 220k, against 4-13 ms between beams at 3-10 m/s), so the speed beams need fast receivers (a few k pull-up, more LED current: the LED only on while active). Delta-t at 40 mm: 4 ms at 10 m/s.
(4) Pairing: the hit (or mouth beam) comes before the counting beam's block by the roll time, about 0.3-0.5 s (mechanical). Take the strongest hit in [block - 1.5 s, block - 0.05 s]. No goal within 1.5 s after a hit = post/bump, dropped. Send it as a nullable shot_speed field on the goal event (contract change later).

## 2026-10-17 13:43  firmware -> electronics
answer (debug OLED, EST, nothing built): (1) Effort small: U8g2 page mode (or Adafruit_SSD1306 + the GFX we already use) ~20-30 kB flash + 0.5/1 kB buffer (128x32/64) on a goal image at 1.25 MB of 3 MB, RAM 46 kB of 320 kB; about a day incl. a Hal show hook + native test, drawn only while awake, shared Wire with the LIS3DH at 100-400 kHz. (2) 0xAE (display off, charge pump stops with it) through deep sleep is fine; panel sleep is µA-level, but the module's LDO + its SDA/SCL pull-ups (in parallel with the LIS3DH's, fine) are the real idle cost: please measure the module in sleep, my guess 5-20 µA = 0.1-0.5 mAh/day. Not gating is right: the lines idle high in deep sleep, nothing drives them low. (3) Show for ~30 s after a wake, then 0xAE (lit OLED ~10-20 mA): battery mV, RSSI + Wi-Fi ok/fail, beam health + mode + margin, last goal seq + age, queue depth, last undo result (applied / too_late ...), config version + table/goal, fw version, device id tail (for registering).

## 2026-10-17 23:51  assembly-review -> electronics
FYI (Li-ion option, if the user picks it): 3 assembly points.
(1) The lid's 2 holder posts + foam (S26) would press on the pouch, and your note says "nothing pressing on it": swap them for a foam-lined frame round the pack's edges, or a flat pad spread over the face, with >= 2 mm swell room.
(2) The 60 × 36 pack in the 69 × 48 pocket slides: it needs corner blocks or foam so it can't reach the board's pins, and its lead strain-relieved.
(3) With D1 bridged, a pack with reversed JST polarity (AliExpress varies) goes straight into the XIAO: make the meter check before first plug-in mandatory in ASSEMBLY, or keep reverse protection (e.g. a P-FET).

## 2026-10-17 23:54  firmware -> electronics
Re pulled battery: unsent goals already live in NVS. Each goal (and undo) is written to the NVS queue before anything is sent, and the write is atomic, so pulling the cells loses no queued goal; they go out on the next wake. RAM loses only the undo ring (after a power cut no goal is inside the 10 s window anyway). OLED noted: built on 0x3C on D4/D5 (board.h OLED_ADDR, 0 = not fitted); U8x8 drives the bus at 400 kHz.

## 2026-10-18 10:58  electronics -> ux
answer: electronics/status-led-2026-10-18.md. GPIO5 (MTDI pad wire, pre-soldered). 3 mm diffused through-hole, not 0603. Green InGaN 525 nm via 220 Ω (≈ 1.5–2 mA) in a socket as the brightness knob. Battery at 2 mA, 30 ms: OK ≈ 0.37, attention ≈ 0.75, batt-low ≈ 1.1 mAh/day (≈ half at 1 mA); your 0.3 holds, §0 unchanged. It must blink via the LP core: HP wakes every 5 s cost ≈ 4–5 mAh/day (firmware).
Red + green on GPIO5 alone: YES, without a Hi-Z leak, IF the green is InGaN (series Vf ≈ 4.1 V > 3.3). LOW = red, HIGH = green, Hi-Z = off. Costs 1 LED, 1 socket and a 3rd wire. Never a yellow-green (it leaks and glows).

## 2026-10-18 10:58  firmware -> ux
Answer (details: firmware/status-led-firmware-2026-10-18.md): blinking in deep sleep = the LP core (recommended; ~1 µA EST of its own, after a half-day spike to check that it links in pioarduino). LP-timer wakes of the main core cost 300-500 µA (a full boot, which doubles the budget), or ~10 µA with a fragile wake stub. Awake-only means dark = asleep or dead, which misses the ask.
Cost at 1 mA / 30 ms: asleep 1 blink / 5 s = 6 µA LED + ~1 µA LP core; awake / 2 s ~ 17 µA. Total about 0.2 mAh/day (+2 %), 0.6 while showing 3 blinks.
One fault function in GoalApp feeds both: the display's B5a verdict, and the LED count (batt low 3 > any other fault 2 > ok 1). Asleep, the count freezes at the last wake's value. No blink at cutoff or on a wrong board.

## 2026-10-18 14:36  assembly-review -> mechanical
ACTION (B16, blocker for the battery contact; found while preparing review 2): the latch lets the pogo pins push the drawer off its contacts. The pins push it outward, so it rests where the latch catches, and the latch has 0.95 of slack along s (bump flank at s ~50.6 vs the notch edge at 49.7). The pins are compressed only 0.75 at the stop, so at the catch they're 0.20 short of touching. The gate's new 'drawer held on its contacts' check fails (gate 133/1).
Fix: hold the drawer AT its stop: notch front edge ~0.9 forward + ~0.1 preload on the arm, or stand-offs set so the catch keeps >= the pin's working compression. 2 pins per pole doubles the push. Details: assembly-review/2026-10-18-review2-gate.md.

Both plan C findings fixed; please turn the KNOWN notes into checks:
1) Hal::oled() is now non-blocking by contract (app.h): the glue hands the latest view to its own draw task at priority 1, and the app (priority 2) preempts it. The bus is busy for ~48 ms per frame, in 25-byte chunks of about 2.3 ms each; only a LIS3DH read can wait, and at most one chunk. Model: oled() costs the tick nothing, and the 3 ms chopped polls continue during a frame, so with the screen on you should get 0/60 misses.
2) The in-ball light is read only while D8 still sees the ball (hal.beamBlocked()) and never in chopped mode, so a late count (ball gone) no longer records lit-node light. Firmware test: test_ball_light_only_while_the_ball_is_in_the_beam.
